items.front: Best first step for any blood-relation puzzle?
items.back: Draw a top-down family tree: elders on top, children below, same generation on one row; fix gender the instant a gendered word appears.
□ = male, ○ = female; horizontal '=' = married couple; vertical '|' = parent→child (descent).

items.front: 'The only daughter of my mother' (said by a woman) resolves to?
items.back: The female speaker herself. 'Only son of my father' (said by a man) = himself. Collapse self-reference first.

items.front: In coded relations, how do you tell maternal from paternal?
items.back: Route through the father = paternal relative; through the mother = maternal. Two people who are both parents of one child are spouses.
items.examPoint: Blood relations — maternal vs paternal side

items.front: Why does 'only son/daughter' matter in a puzzle?
items.back: It blocks any cousin/aunt/uncle branch on that side, usually forcing the chain to the speaker's own parent or the speaker.
1 link = parent, 2 = grandparent, 3 = great-grandparent. Spouse's parent = parent-in-law; daughter's husband = son-in-law.

items.front: The decisive check in a data-sufficiency blood-relation item?
items.back: Is the target person's GENDER fixed? 'Child/parent/cousin/spouse' are gender-neutral; a statement can fix the tree yet stay insufficient.
items.source: APPSC Group-1 — Data Sufficiency in Blood Relation

items.front: Linear seating: where to start, and the facing rule?
items.back: Fix the most-constrained seat (often the middle) first. Facing north → person's left = observer's left; facing south flips left/right.

items.front: Circular seating (facing centre): left-right & opposite equivalence for n seats?
items.back: 'k to the left' = '(n−k) to the right'; the exactly-opposite seat is n/2 places away (only when n is even).
items.examPoint: Seating — circular arrangement: opposite and left-right equivalence

items.front: Ranking: total people when one person's positions from both ends are given?
items.back: Total = L + R − 1 (the person is counted from both ends). Position from other end = N − (this-end position) + 1.
items.examPoint: Ranking — total persons from positions from both ends

items.front: Ranking on interchange of two persons' seats?
items.back: Each person takes the other's fixed position; then total = (new position from left) + (that seat's position from right) − 1.
